text: 莫谓书生空议论，头颅掷处血斑斑
pinyin: mò wèi shū shēng kōng yì lùn, tóu lú zhì chù xuè bān bān
variants: 莫道书生空议论，头颅掷处血斑斑
literal: don't · say · scholar · empty · talk, head · thrown · place · blood · spotted
natural: do not call a scholar's words empty talk; where heads were thrown down, blood still stains the ground

meaning.en: A couplet in praise of scholars who put their lives behind their words: do not dismiss intellectuals as mere talkers, for some paid for their views with their heads.
meaning.zh: 称赞读书人言行一致、敢于献身的名句：不要说书生只会空谈，他们有人是用头颅和鲜血来践行主张的。

equivalents: don't dismiss scholars as mere talkers
words backed with blood

examples.zh: 他在讲座结尾引用“莫谓书生空议论，头颅掷处血斑斑”，赞扬东林党人的气节。
examples.en: He closed the lecture with 'do not call a scholar's words empty talk; blood stains where heads were thrown', praising the integrity of the Donglin men.

examples.zh: 有人讥笑知识分子只会清谈，他便回了一句“莫谓书生空议论，头颅掷处血斑斑”。
examples.en: When someone sneered that intellectuals only talk, he answered with 'do not call a scholar's words empty talk'.

story.en: The Donglin Academy in Wuxi was the centre of the late-Ming Donglin movement, whose members criticised the court and several died in prison or under torture. The quatrain is traditionally credited to Deng Tuo (1912-1966), who visited the academy in 1960; its title and wording are not identical in every source.
story.zh: 无锡东林书院是明末东林运动的中心，东林人士批评朝政，数人惨死狱中。此诗一般认为是邓拓（1912—1966）1960年参观东林书院时所作，诗题和个别字句在各书中不尽一致。

date.zh: 中华人民共和国 · 约1961年

usage.en: Quoted to defend the courage and integrity of scholars. The couplet is the second half of a quatrain whose first line is 东林讲学继龟山，事事关心天下间. It is usually credited to Deng Tuo, who is said to have written it on visiting the Donglin Academy in Wuxi in 1960; the poem's exact title and occasion vary between sources, and some print 莫道 for 莫谓.
usage.zh: 常用来为读书人的气节和担当辩护。这是一首七绝的后两句，前两句为“东林讲学继龟山，事事关心天下间”。一般认为是邓拓1960年游无锡东林书院时所作，诗题和写作情形各书说法略有不同，个别版本“莫谓”作“莫道”。

text: 文章满纸书生累，风雨同舟战友贤
pinyin: wén zhāng mǎn zhǐ shū shēng lèi, fēng yǔ tóng zhōu zhàn yǒu xián
literal: writings · fill · paper · scholar · burden, wind · rain · same · boat · comrade · worthy
natural: pages full of writing are a scholar's burden; comrades who shared the storm in one boat were worthy

meaning.en: A farewell couplet: a scholar's life of writing is a heavy burden, but he was lucky to have worthy comrades beside him through hard times.
meaning.zh: 告别之作中的一联：读书人满纸文章，难免劳累，所幸一路有风雨同舟的贤良战友。

equivalents: a writer's toil, a comrade's loyalty
side by side through storm and stress

examples.zh: 退休那天，老编辑在留言簿上写下“文章满纸书生累，风雨同舟战友贤”。
examples.en: On the day he retired the old editor wrote in the guestbook, 'pages of writing are a scholar's burden; comrades who shared the storm were worthy'.

examples.zh: 毕业纪念册里，他抄了一句“文章满纸书生累，风雨同舟战友贤”送给同事。
examples.en: In the farewell album he copied out 'pages of writing are a scholar's burden; comrades who shared the storm were worthy' for his colleagues.

origin.source: 邓拓《留别人民日报诸同志》（1959年）

story.en: Deng Tuo wrote the poem in February 1959 when he left the editor-in-chief's post at the People's Daily after about ten years; it opens '笔走龙蛇二十年，分明非梦亦非烟'.
story.zh: 1959年2月，邓拓卸任《人民日报》总编辑之职，作此诗留别同仁；诗的开头是“笔走龙蛇二十年，分明非梦亦非烟”。

usage.en: Quoted in farewells between colleagues, especially in journalism and publishing. 风雨同舟 is also a common idiom with its own entry. The couplet is the middle of an eight-line poem that opens 笔走龙蛇二十年，分明非梦亦非烟.
usage.zh: 多用于同事、战友之间话别，在新闻出版界尤其常见。“风雨同舟”本身也是常用成语，另有词条。这一联出自一首八句的诗，开头是“笔走龙蛇二十年，分明非梦亦非烟”。

text: 伟大的空话
pinyin: wěi dà de kōng huà
literal: great · 's · empty · talk
natural: grand empty talk

meaning.en: Deng Tuo's ironic title for talk that is full of lofty slogans but says nothing practical.
meaning.zh: 邓拓杂文的题目，讽刺那种口号响亮、内容空洞、于事无补的话。

equivalents: grand but empty talk
lofty-sounding hot air

examples.zh: 这份讲话稿通篇口号，简直是一篇伟大的空话。
examples.en: The speech is slogans from start to finish, nothing but grand empty talk.

examples.zh: 开会不讨论办法，只喊口号，那就成了伟大的空话。
examples.en: If a meeting only shouts slogans instead of discussing solutions, it becomes grand empty talk.

origin.source: 邓拓《燕山夜话·伟大的空话》（1961年）

story.en: 'Great Empty Talk' is one of the short essays Deng Tuo wrote for 《燕山夜话》 (Evening Chats at Yanshan), which ran in the Beijing Evening News from 1961; it mocks speech full of grand words and no content.
story.zh: 《伟大的空话》是邓拓为《北京晚报》专栏《燕山夜话》（1961年起）所写的杂文之一，嘲讽满篇大话而没有实际内容的言论。

usage.en: Used ironically, in writing and speech, for pompous, slogan-filled statements without substance. It comes from the title of an essay in Deng Tuo's column 《燕山夜话》 (1961), written under the pen name Ma Nancun.
usage.zh: 多作宾语或定语，带讽刺意味，形容空泛而夸大的话。语出邓拓以“马南邨”为笔名发表的《燕山夜话》（1961年）中的一篇杂文题目。

text: 一个鸡蛋的家当
pinyin: yī gè jī dàn de jiā dang
literal: one · egg · 's · family · property
natural: a whole fortune from one egg

meaning.en: The title of a Deng Tuo essay retelling the story of a poor man who dreams of growing rich from a single egg, then ruins it by getting carried away.
meaning.zh: 邓拓杂文的题目，讲的是穷人幻想靠一个鸡蛋发家致富、得意忘形而把鸡蛋摔碎的故事，讽刺不切实际的空想。

equivalents: counting your chickens before they hatch
castles in the air

examples.zh: 他还没拿到订单就盘算着开分公司，真是一个鸡蛋的家当。
examples.en: He was planning branch offices before he had a single order, a whole fortune counted out of one egg.

examples.zh: 别做一个鸡蛋的家当式的白日梦，先把手头的事做好。
examples.en: Don't daydream a fortune out of one egg; do the job in front of you first.

origin.source: 邓拓《燕山夜话·一个鸡蛋的家当》

story.en: Deng Tuo's essay retells a story from Jiang Yingke's 《雪涛小说》 (Ming dynasty): a poor man imagines that the egg he owns will hatch a chick, which will lay eggs, and so on until he is rich, and in his excitement he smashes the egg.
story.zh: 邓拓的这篇杂文改写自明代江盈科《雪涛小说》中的故事：穷人设想一个鸡蛋孵出小鸡，小鸡再生蛋，如此循环便能发财，得意忘形之际把鸡蛋打碎了。

date.zh: 中华人民共和国 · 约1961年

usage.en: Used for wishful thinking that builds a grand future on a tiny, uncertain start. The story is told in an essay in 《燕山夜话》; Deng Tuo took it from the Ming writer Jiang Yingke's 《雪涛小说》. The English equivalents are the closest analogues, not exact translations.
usage.zh: 形容在微不足道、毫无把握的基础上空想发财。故事见于《燕山夜话》中的一篇杂文，邓拓取材于明代江盈科的《雪涛小说》。

text: 天下之治乱，不在一姓之兴亡，而在万民之忧乐
pinyin: tiān xià zhī zhì luàn, bù zài yī xìng zhī xīng wáng, ér zài wàn mín zhī yōu lè
literal: world · 's · order · disorder, not · lie in · one · surname · 's · rise · fall, but · lie in · ten thousand · people · 's · sorrow · joy
natural: whether the world is well ruled lies not in the rise and fall of one family, but in the sorrow and joy of the people

meaning.en: Huang Zongxi's test of good government: look not at whether a dynasty survives, but at whether ordinary people are happy or suffering.
meaning.zh: 黄宗羲论治乱的标准：天下太平与否，不看哪一个王朝兴亡，而看百姓是忧是乐。

equivalents: a state is judged by its people's welfare, not its dynasty's survival
the people's wellbeing is the measure of good rule

examples.zh: 评价一个时代，应该像黄宗羲说的那样，“天下之治乱，不在一姓之兴亡，而在万民之忧乐”。
examples.en: A period should be judged as Huang Zongxi said: order or disorder lies not in one family's rise and fall but in the people's sorrow and joy.

examples.zh: 社论引用“天下之治乱，不在一姓之兴亡，而在万民之忧乐”，呼吁关注民生。
examples.en: The editorial quoted 'order or disorder lies not in one family's rise and fall but in the people's sorrow and joy' to call for attention to livelihood.

origin.source: 黄宗羲《明夷待访录·原臣》

story.en: In the chapter 'On Ministers' (《原臣》) Huang Zongxi argues that a minister's duty is to the people, not to a single ruler or family; the line begins '盖天下之治乱…'.
story.zh: 黄宗羲在《原臣》篇中指出，臣子的职责在于天下万民，而不在君主一人一姓；此句开头为“盖天下之治乱……”。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of governance and of people-centred values. 一姓 means one ruling family or dynasty. Literary and formal.
usage.zh: 常在谈论治理和以民为本的价值时引用。“一姓”指一个王朝或一个统治家族。书面、庄重。

synonyms: 民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻

text: 天下惟器而已矣
pinyin: tiān xià wéi qì ér yǐ yǐ
literal: world · only · vessels · that's all
natural: in the world there are only concrete things, nothing more

meaning.en: Wang Fuzhi's thesis that what exists in the world is concrete things (器); the 'Way' (道) is found in them, not apart from them.
meaning.zh: 王夫之的哲学命题：天下所存在的只是具体的事物（器），“道”存在于器之中，而不是脱离器的东西。

equivalents: there is nothing but concrete things
principle lives in things, not above them

examples.zh: 讲到中国哲学史，老师特别提到王夫之的“天下惟器而已矣”。
examples.en: In the lecture on Chinese philosophy the teacher singled out Wang Fuzhi's 'in the world there are only concrete things'.

examples.zh: 他用“天下惟器而已矣”来说明，道理不能脱离实际事物。
examples.en: He used 'in the world there are only concrete things' to show that principle cannot be separated from real things.

story.en: Wang Fuzhi (1619-1692), a thinker of the Ming-Qing transition, wrote this in his 《周易外传》 (Outer Commentary on the Book of Changes), commenting on the Appended Words.
story.zh: 王夫之（1619—1692）为明清之际思想家，此语见于其《周易外传》，是对《系辞》的阐发。

usage.en: A philosophical formula, quoted in histories of thought. The next clause reads 道者器之道，器者不可谓之道之器也 ('the Way is the way of things, not things the things of the Way'). 器 literally means a vessel or utensil. Formal and literary.
usage.zh: 哲学命题，多见于思想史著作。下文为“道者器之道，器者不可谓之道之器也”。“器”本义为器具，这里指具体的事物。书面、庄重。

text: 天下有定理而无定法
pinyin: tiān xià yǒu dìng lǐ ér wú dìng fǎ
literal: world · have · fixed · principle · but · lack · fixed · method
natural: there are fixed principles in the world, but no fixed methods

meaning.en: Principles stay constant, but the way to apply them must change with the situation.
meaning.zh: 道理是固定的，但运用的方法没有一成不变的，要因时因地而变。

equivalents: principles are fixed, methods are flexible
there is more than one way to skin a cat

examples.zh: 天下有定理而无定法，同样的原则在不同的场合要用不同的做法。
examples.en: There are fixed principles but no fixed methods; the same principle calls for different actions in different settings.

examples.zh: 写作如此，教学也如此，天下有定理而无定法。
examples.en: So it is with writing, so it is with teaching: principles are fixed, methods are not.

usage.en: Often credited to Wang Fuzhi, but I could not confirm the exact source, so no origin or period is given. Used in discussions of teaching, writing, management and strategy.
usage.zh: 常被说成是王夫之的话，但具体出处未能确证，故不标出处和朝代。多用于谈论教学、写作、管理和谋略。

text: 唯天下之至诚能胜天下之至伪，唯天下之至拙能胜天下之至巧
pinyin: wéi tiān xià zhī zhì chéng néng shèng tiān xià zhī zhì wěi, wéi tiān xià zhī zhì zhuō néng shèng tiān xià zhī zhì qiǎo
variants: 惟天下之至诚能胜天下之至伪，惟天下之至拙能胜天下之至巧
literal: only · world · 's · utmost · sincerity · can · defeat · world · 's · utmost · falsehood, only · world · 's · utmost · clumsiness · can · defeat · world · 's · utmost · cleverness
natural: only the most sincere in the world can beat the most false; only the most plodding can beat the most clever

meaning.en: Zeng Guofan's creed: complete sincerity defeats cunning, and honest, unglamorous persistence beats cleverness in the end.
meaning.zh: 曾国藩的信条：至诚能战胜虚伪，朴拙踏实的坚持终究能胜过取巧。

equivalents: honesty is the best policy
slow and steady wins the race

examples.zh: 他信奉“唯天下之至诚能胜天下之至伪，唯天下之至拙能胜天下之至巧”，做事从不耍小聪明。
examples.en: He lived by 'only utter sincerity can beat utter falsehood, only utter plodding can beat utter cleverness' and never played smart tricks.

examples.zh: 读《曾国藩家书》，最让人记住的是“唯天下之至诚能胜天下之至伪，唯天下之至拙能胜天下之至巧”一句。
examples.en: What stays in the mind from Zeng Guofan's letters is 'only utter sincerity can beat utter falsehood, only utter plodding can beat utter cleverness'.

usage.en: Commonly credited to Zeng Guofan and quoted as his creed for dealing with people and work; the exact source passage is not confirmed here, so no origin is given. Often written with 惟 instead of 唯. 拙 means clumsy, plain, unshowy, not stupid.
usage.zh: 一般认为是曾国藩的话，常被当作他为人处事的信条；具体出处此处未能确证，故不标出处。“唯”也常写作“惟”。“拙”指朴拙、不取巧，并非愚笨。

text: 不为圣贤，便为禽兽
pinyin: bù wéi shèng xián, biàn wéi qín shòu
literal: not · become · sage · worthy, then · become · bird · beast
natural: if you do not become a sage, you become a beast

meaning.en: Zeng Guofan's stern motto on self-cultivation: aim at being a sage; if you do not, you will sink to the level of an animal.
meaning.zh: 曾国藩立志修身的严厉格言：要立志做圣贤，否则就会堕落得像禽兽一样。

equivalents: aim for the heights or sink to the depths
no middle way in self-cultivation

examples.zh: 他把“不为圣贤，便为禽兽”写在日记扉页，时时提醒自己。
examples.en: He wrote 'if not a sage, then a beast' on the flyleaf of his diary as a constant reminder.

examples.zh: 曾国藩常说“不为圣贤，便为禽兽”，要求自己和子弟立大志。
examples.en: Zeng Guofan often said 'if not a sage, then a beast', urging himself and his sons to set high aims.

usage.en: Commonly credited to Zeng Guofan's diary and family letters; the exact passage is not confirmed here, and similar rhetoric already appears in Neo-Confucian writing, so no origin is given. Stark and moralistic; quoted when discussing self-discipline and ambition.
usage.zh: 一般认为见于曾国藩日记和家书，具体篇目此处未能确证，类似的说法在理学著作中早已有之，故不标出处。语气严厉，带说教色彩，多在谈论自律和志向时引用。

text: 保国、保教、保种
pinyin: bǎo guó, bǎo jiào, bǎo zhǒng
literal: protect · state, protect · teaching, protect · race
natural: protect the state, protect the teaching, protect the race

meaning.en: Late-Qing slogan for national survival: preserve the state, preserve the Confucian teaching and preserve the Chinese people.
meaning.zh: 清末救亡的口号：保住国家，保住圣教（儒家学说），保住华夏种族。

equivalents: save the nation, its creed and its people
national survival slogan

examples.zh: 讲清末思想史时，老师常提到“保国、保教、保种”这个口号。
examples.en: In lessons on late-Qing thought the teacher often mentions the slogan 'protect the state, the teaching and the race'.

examples.zh: 张之洞在《劝学篇》中提出“保国、保教、保种”，希望在变局中守住根本。
examples.en: In 'An Exhortation to Learning' Zhang Zhidong put forward 'protect the state, the teaching and the race', hoping to hold on to the essentials in a time of upheaval.

story.en: Zhang Zhidong (1837-1909) opened his 《劝学篇》 of 1898 by saying that to meet the crisis one must protect the state, the sacred teaching and the Chinese race (保国家、保圣教、保华种).
story.zh: 张之洞（1837—1909）在1898年的《劝学篇》序中提出，应对危局须“保国家、保圣教、保华种”。

usage.en: A historical slogan of the 1890s, used today when discussing the reform movement and its debates. 教 means the Confucian teaching and 种 the Chinese people, in the terms of the day. Kang Youwei's Society for the Protection of the Nation (保国会, 1898) used the same three aims, usually ordered 保国、保种、保教.
usage.zh: 1890年代的历史口号，今天多在谈论维新运动及其争论时使用。“教”指儒家圣教，“种”指华夏民族，皆为当时用语。康有为1898年组织的保国会也提出同样的三项宗旨，通常写作“保国、保种、保教”。

text: 练兵也，海军也，都是纸糊的老虎
pinyin: liàn bīng yě, hǎi jūn yě, dōu shì zhǐ hú de lǎo hǔ
literal: train troops · also, navy · also, all · are · paper · pasted · 's · tiger
natural: army training and the navy alike are paper tigers

meaning.en: Li Hongzhang's bitter admission that the army and navy he had built for decades looked strong but would not survive a real test.
meaning.zh: 李鸿章的感叹：他办了一辈子的练兵和海军，看上去威风，实际上经不起真正的考验。

equivalents: a paper tiger
all show and no substance

examples.zh: 他在回忆录里引用李鸿章“练兵也，海军也，都是纸糊的老虎”，说明晚清军备的虚弱。
examples.en: In his memoir he quoted Li Hongzhang's 'army training and the navy alike are paper tigers' to show how weak late-Qing defences were.

examples.zh: 讲甲午战争时，老师引用了“练兵也，海军也，都是纸糊的老虎”这句话。
examples.en: When teaching the First Sino-Japanese War the teacher quoted 'army training and the navy alike are paper tigers'.

story.en: Li Hongzhang (1823-1901) built the Beiyang army and fleet; the remark is recorded in Wu Yong's 《庚子西狩丛谈》 (Notes on the Western Flight of 1900): '我办了一辈子的事，练兵也，海军也，都是纸糊的老虎，何尝能实在放手办理'.
story.zh: 李鸿章（1823—1901）一手创建北洋陆海军；此话载于吴永《庚子西狩丛谈》：“我办了一辈子的事，练兵也，海军也，都是纸糊的老虎，何尝能实在放手办理。”

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of late-Qing modernisation and the 1894-95 war. The wording follows Wu Yong's account, in which Li continues '何尝能实在放手办理' ('how could I ever carry it out in earnest'); as a recollected remark, the exact words may differ from what Li said.
usage.zh: 多在谈论晚清洋务和甲午战争时引用。字句依据吴永的记述，下文接“何尝能实在放手办理”；既是追记的谈话，与李鸿章当时的原话可能略有出入。

text: 公理之未明，即以革命明之；旧俗之俱在，即以革命去之
pinyin: gōng lǐ zhī wèi míng, jí yǐ gé mìng míng zhī, jiù sú zhī jù zài, jí yǐ gé mìng qù zhī
literal: public · principle · 's · not yet · clear, then · by · revolution · make clear · it; old · customs · 's · all · remain, then · by · revolution · remove · it
natural: if justice is not yet clear, make it clear by revolution; if old customs all remain, sweep them away by revolution

meaning.en: Zhang Taiyan's argument that revolution is the means both to establish what is right and to clear away outworn custom.
meaning.zh: 章太炎的主张：革命既是彰明公理的手段，也是铲除陈旧习俗的手段。

equivalents: revolution to clarify right and abolish old ways
clear away the old by revolution

examples.zh: 课上讲到辛亥革命前的思想论争，引用了“公理之未明，即以革命明之；旧俗之俱在，即以革命去之”。
examples.en: The class on the debates before the 1911 Revolution quoted 'if justice is not yet clear, make it clear by revolution; if old customs remain, remove them by revolution'.

examples.zh: 这篇文章的气势，正如章太炎所说“公理之未明，即以革命明之；旧俗之俱在，即以革命去之”。
examples.en: The force of the essay is just as Zhang Taiyan put it: 'if justice is not yet clear, make it clear by revolution'.

origin.source: 章太炎《驳康有为论革命书》（1903年）

story.en: In 1903 Zhang Taiyan (1869-1936) published an open letter answering Kang Youwei's argument that China should reform rather than rebel; it is one of the best-known texts of the revolutionary camp.
story.zh: 1903年，章太炎（1869—1936）发表此文，驳斥康有为主张“只可改良、不可革命”的观点，是革命派最著名的文章之一。

usage.en: A historical quotation from the revolutionary polemics of the early 1900s; read it as a statement of its time. Literary, in a balanced classical couplet.
usage.zh: 清末革命论战中的名句，应当放在当时的历史背景下理解。书面语，对偶句式。

text: 法者天下之公器，变者天下之公理
pinyin: fǎ zhě tiān xià zhī gōng qì, biàn zhě tiān xià zhī gōng lǐ
variants: 法者，天下之公器也；变者，天下之公理也
literal: law · that · world · 's · public · instrument, change · that · world · 's · public · principle
natural: law is the common instrument of the world, and change is its common principle

meaning.en: Liang Qichao's reasoning for reform: laws belong to everyone, and change is a universal rule, so laws must change with the times.
meaning.zh: 梁启超为变法所作的论证：法律是天下人共有的工具，变化是天下共通的规律，所以法度必须随时代而变。

equivalents: laws must change with the times
change is the law of all things

examples.zh: 他引用“法者天下之公器，变者天下之公理”，说明修改旧规定是应有之义。
examples.en: He quoted 'law is the common instrument of the world, change its common principle' to show that revising old rules is only natural.

examples.zh: 梁启超在《变法通议》里写道：“法者天下之公器，变者天下之公理。”
examples.en: Liang Qichao wrote in 'On Reform': 'law is the common instrument of the world, change its common principle'.

story.en: Liang Qichao (1873-1929) published 《变法通议》 (General Discussion of Reform) in the journal 《时务报》 from 1896; the line comes from the opening, which argues that all things and all laws must change.
story.zh: 梁启超（1873—1929）自1896年起在《时务报》连载《变法通议》，此句出自开篇，论述天下万物、一切法度都须变化。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of law reform and the 1898 reform movement. The original reads 法者，天下之公器也；变者，天下之公理也, which is listed as a variant. 公器 means a thing shared by all.
usage.zh: 多在谈论法律变革和戊戌变法时引用。原文作“法者，天下之公器也；变者，天下之公理也”，列为异形。“公器”指天下人共有之物。

text: 一腔热血勤珍重，洒去犹能化碧涛
pinyin: yī qiāng rè xuè qín zhēn zhòng, sǎ qù yóu néng huà bì tāo
literal: one · chest · hot · blood · diligently · cherish, spilled · away · still · can · turn into · green · waves
natural: guard your hot blood well; spilled, it can still turn to green waves

meaning.en: Qiu Jin's vow of sacrifice: cherish the blood in your heart, for if it must be shed, it will still become something lasting and clean.
meaning.zh: 秋瑾表达献身志向的诗句：要珍重胸中的热血，即使洒出，也能化作碧波，永不消逝。

equivalents: blood shed for a cause is never in vain
a life offered to a great cause

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长朗诵了“一腔热血勤珍重，洒去犹能化碧涛”。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the principal recited 'guard your hot blood well; spilled, it can still turn to green waves'.

examples.zh: 参观秋瑾故居时，讲解员念起了“一腔热血勤珍重，洒去犹能化碧涛”。
examples.en: On the visit to Qiu Jin's former home the guide recited 'guard your hot blood well; spilled, it can still turn to green waves'.

story.en: The last couplet of Qiu Jin's poem 'Facing the Wine' (《对酒》), whose opening couplet is '不惜千金买宝刀，貂裘换酒也堪豪'. Qiu Jin (1875-1907) was executed after a failed uprising.
story.zh: 秋瑾《对酒》的末联，前一联为“不惜千金买宝刀，貂裘换酒也堪豪”。秋瑾（1875—1907）因起义失败被害。

usage.en: Quoted for patriotic and self-sacrificing resolve, and in talks on Qiu Jin. The 碧 refers to the old belief that the blood of a loyal man turns to green jade (化碧, from the story of Chang Hong in 《庄子》). Literary; the line completes the poem whose opening couplet is the existing entry 不惜千金买宝刀，貂裘换酒也堪豪.
usage.zh: 用于表达爱国、献身的志向，也常在介绍秋瑾时引用。“化碧”用忠臣之血三年化为碧玉的典故（苌弘事，见《庄子》）。书面语；这一联与“不惜千金买宝刀，貂裘换酒也堪豪”同出一诗。

text: 青年如初春，如朝日，如百卉之萌动
pinyin: qīng nián rú chū chūn, rú zhāo rì, rú bǎi huì zhī méng dòng
literal: youth · like · early · spring, like · morning · sun, like · hundred · plants · 's · sprouting
natural: youth is like early spring, like the morning sun, like a hundred plants beginning to sprout

meaning.en: Chen Duxiu's picture of youth: fresh, rising and full of the energy of new growth.
meaning.zh: 陈独秀对青年的比喻：像初春，像朝阳，像百草萌发，充满新生的活力。

equivalents: youth is the spring of life
the morning of life

examples.zh: 新生入学典礼上，学长朗读了“青年如初春，如朝日，如百卉之萌动”。
examples.en: At the freshers' ceremony a senior read out 'youth is like early spring, like the morning sun, like a hundred plants beginning to sprout'.

examples.zh: 作文里引用“青年如初春，如朝日，如百卉之萌动”，一下子显得有气势。
examples.en: Quoting 'youth is like early spring, like the morning sun, like a hundred plants beginning to sprout' gave the essay instant momentum.

story.en: Chen Duxiu (1879-1942) published 'A Call to Youth' (《敬告青年》) in the first issue of 《青年杂志》 in September 1915, the magazine that became 《新青年》 and led the New Culture Movement.
story.zh: 1915年9月，陈独秀（1879—1942）在《青年杂志》创刊号发表《敬告青年》；该刊后改名《新青年》，成为新文化运动的旗帜。

usage.en: A favourite for essays and speeches about young people. The original continues 如利刃之新发于硎，人生最可宝贵之时期也. 朝 here is zhāo, 'morning'; 卉 means plants.
usage.zh: 常用于有关青年的作文和演讲。原文接下去是“如利刃之新发于硎，人生最可宝贵之时期也”。“朝日”的“朝”读 zhāo；“卉”指花草。

text: 交换、比较、反复
pinyin: jiāo huàn, bǐ jiào, fǎn fù
literal: exchange, compare, repeat
natural: exchange views, compare, repeat

meaning.en: Chen Yun's three-step method for reaching sound judgements: swap opinions with others, compare the alternatives, and go over the matter again and again.
meaning.zh: 陈云提出的三步判断方法：与人交换意见，对不同方案进行比较，对问题反复考虑。

equivalents: discuss, compare, review
look at it from every side, again and again

examples.zh: 做决策时要坚持“交换、比较、反复”，不能拍脑袋。
examples.en: In making decisions we must hold to 'exchange, compare, repeat' and not decide off the cuff.

examples.zh: 他的工作方法就是交换、比较、反复，所以很少出错。
examples.en: His method of work is exchange, compare, repeat, which is why he seldom makes mistakes.

usage.en: The phrase is usually quoted together with 不唯上，不唯书，只唯实 as a short summary of Chen Yun's approach to decision-making; it is quoted in the press and in training materials. The exact occasion of its first statement is not given here, so no origin is added.
usage.zh: 常与“不唯上，不唯书，只唯实”并称，概括陈云的决策方法，见于报刊和干部培训材料。最初提出的具体场合此处不作说明，故不标出处。

text: 试看将来的环球，必是赤旗的世界
pinyin: shì kàn jiāng lái de huán qiú, bì shì chì qí de shì jiè
literal: try · look · future · 's · globe, surely · be · red · flag · 's · world
natural: look at the world to come: it will surely be a world of the red flag

meaning.en: Li Dazhao's prediction, made soon after the Russian Revolution and the end of the First World War, that the future world would belong to the red flag of socialism.
meaning.zh: 李大钊在俄国革命和一战结束之后作出的预言：将来的世界必将是社会主义红旗的世界。

equivalents: the future belongs to the red flag
the shape of the coming world

examples.zh: 展厅里陈列着李大钊的名句：“试看将来的环球，必是赤旗的世界。”
examples.en: The exhibition hall displayed Li Dazhao's famous line, 'look at the world to come: it will surely be a world of the red flag'.

examples.zh: 课文引用“试看将来的环球，必是赤旗的世界”，说明早期共产主义者的信念。
examples.en: The text quotes 'look at the world to come: it will surely be a world of the red flag' to show the conviction of early communists.

story.en: Li Dazhao (1889-1927) wrote 'The Victory of Bolshevism' in November 1918 for 《新青年》, after the Russian October Revolution and the Armistice; the sentence is its famous conclusion.
story.zh: 李大钊（1889—1927）1918年11月在《新青年》发表《Bolshevism的胜利》，当时俄国十月革命刚刚成功，一战也刚刚结束；这句话是文中的名句。

usage.en: Cited today as a historical statement of early Chinese Marxists' faith, in textbooks, museums and commemorations. It is a prediction, not a description of the present. 环球 means the whole globe; 赤旗 the red flag.
usage.zh: 今天多作为早期中国马克思主义者信念的历史表述，见于教科书、展览和纪念文章。这是对未来的预言，并非对现状的描述。“环球”指全世界，“赤旗”即红旗。

text: 青年者，人生之王，人生之春，人生之华也
pinyin: qīng nián zhě, rén shēng zhī wáng, rén shēng zhī chūn, rén shēng zhī huá yě
literal: youth · that, life · 's · king, life · 's · spring, life · 's · flower · [particle]
natural: youth is the king of life, the spring of life, the flower of life

meaning.en: Li Dazhao's praise of youth as the best and most powerful stage of a person's life.
meaning.zh: 李大钊对青春的赞美：青年时期是人生最宝贵、最有力量的阶段。

equivalents: youth is the best season of life
the flower of life is youth

examples.zh: 毕业纪念册的扉页上印着“青年者，人生之王，人生之春，人生之华也”。
examples.en: The flyleaf of the graduation album bore 'youth is the king, the spring, the flower of life'.

examples.zh: 演讲稿开头引用了“青年者，人生之王，人生之春，人生之华也”。
examples.en: The speech opened with 'youth is the king of life, the spring of life, the flower of life'.

story.en: Li Dazhao wrote 'Youth' (《青春》) for the first issue of volume 2 of 《新青年》 in September 1916; the essay urges the young to throw off the old and build a new, young China.
story.zh: 1916年9月，李大钊为《新青年》第2卷第1号撰写《青春》一文，号召青年摆脱陈腐，创造青春的中国。

usage.en: A favourite in speeches and essays about youth. In the original it continues with a passage about how to make good use of youth. 华 here means 'flower, bloom' (huá).
usage.zh: 常用于有关青春和青年的演讲与作文。原文接着论述如何善用青春。“华”在这里指花、精华。

text: 最是人间留不住，朱颜辞镜花辞树
pinyin: zuì shì rén jiān liú bù zhù, zhū yán cí jìng huā cí shù
literal: most · is · human · world · keep · not · stay, rosy · face · leave · mirror · flowers · leave · tree
natural: what the world can least hold: a youthful face leaving the mirror, blossoms leaving the tree

meaning.en: The closing lines of a Wang Guowei lyric: youth and beauty cannot be kept, any more than blossoms can stay on the branch.
meaning.zh: 王国维词的结尾：青春容颜和花朵一样，都留不住，终要离开镜子、离开枝头。

equivalents: youth and beauty cannot be kept
time takes the bloom from face and flower

examples.zh: 读到“最是人间留不住，朱颜辞镜花辞树”，她不禁想起了逝去的青春。
examples.en: Reading 'what the world can least hold: a face leaving the mirror, blossoms leaving the tree', she thought of her vanished youth.

examples.zh: 他在日记里抄下“最是人间留不住，朱颜辞镜花辞树”，感叹时光匆匆。
examples.en: He copied 'what the world can least hold: a face leaving the mirror, blossoms leaving the tree' into his diary, sighing at how fast time goes.

origin.source: 王国维《蝶恋花·阅尽天涯离别苦》

story.en: The last two lines of Wang Guowei's lyric to the tune 蝶恋花, which opens '阅尽天涯离别苦'; it is included in his 《人间词》.
story.zh: 王国维《蝶恋花》（阅尽天涯离别苦）的结尾两句，收入其《人间词》。

usage.en: Quoted when lamenting passing time and fading youth; wistful, literary. 朱颜 means a rosy, youthful complexion. The lyric (to the tune 蝶恋花) is from 《人间词》.
usage.zh: 用于感叹时光流逝、青春不再，带惆怅意味，书面语。“朱颜”指红润的青春容颜。这首词（词牌《蝶恋花》）出自《人间词》。

text: 吾曹不出，如苍生何
pinyin: wú cáo bù chū, rú cāng shēng hé
literal: we · not · come forth, how · common people · be
natural: if we do not step forward, what will become of the people?

meaning.en: A call to those with ability to take public responsibility: if the capable stay aloof, the common people will suffer.
meaning.zh: 呼吁有才能的人出来担起社会责任：如果有本事的人都置身事外，百姓怎么办？

equivalents: if not us, who?
what will become of the people if we stay out of it?

examples.zh: 面对灾情，志愿者们说：“吾曹不出，如苍生何？”
examples.en: Facing the disaster the volunteers said, 'if we do not step forward, what will become of the people?'

examples.zh: 他辞去闲职，投身乡村教育，自称“吾曹不出，如苍生何”。
examples.en: He gave up a comfortable post for rural education, saying 'if we do not step forward, what will become of the people?'

usage.en: A recast of the old line 安石不出，将如苍生何, said of the statesman Xie An (《世说新语·排调》). Liang Shuming is known to have adopted the adapted form as his own motto, but the exact occasion is not confirmed here, so no origin is given. 吾曹 means 'we, people like us'.
usage.zh: 改自“安石不出，将如苍生何”（指谢安，见《世说新语·排调》）。一般认为梁漱溟曾以改后的句子自励，但具体场合此处未能确证，故不标出处。“吾曹”意为“我们这些人”。

text: 我是一条天狗呀
pinyin: wǒ shì yī tiáo tiān gǒu yā
literal: I · am · one · [measure word] · heavenly · dog · [exclamation]
natural: I am a heavenly hound!

meaning.en: The opening line of Guo Moruo's poem 'The Heavenly Hound': a bold cry of limitless energy, the poet swallowing moon, sun and the whole universe.
meaning.zh: 郭沫若诗《天狗》的开头：诗人以吞下日月星辰乃至整个宇宙的天狗自喻，高呼无拘无束、力量无穷的自我。

equivalents: I am a force of nature
a cry of boundless self

examples.zh: 朗诵会上，他用尽全力喊出“我是一条天狗呀”。
examples.en: At the recital he shouted 'I am a heavenly hound!' with all his strength.

examples.zh: 语文课上讲到《天狗》，同学们齐声朗读“我是一条天狗呀”。
examples.en: In the Chinese lesson on 'The Heavenly Hound' the class read 'I am a heavenly hound!' aloud together.

story.en: Guo Moruo (1892-1978) wrote 'The Heavenly Hound' in 1920 and gathered it in his collection 《女神》 (The Goddesses, 1921), a landmark of modern Chinese free verse.
story.zh: 郭沫若（1892—1978）1920年作《天狗》，收入诗集《女神》（1921年），是中国现代自由体诗的代表作。

usage.en: A symbol of the unbridled, self-assertive spirit of the May Fourth era. The 天狗 is the mythical dog said to swallow the sun and moon in an eclipse. Quoted in literary studies and school recitals; the line is exclamatory in tone.
usage.zh: 五四时期奔放、自我张扬精神的象征。“天狗”是传说中吞食日月（日食、月食）的神犬。多见于文学研究和校园朗诵，语气为感叹。

text: 我是天空里的一片云，偶尔投影在你的波心
pinyin: wǒ shì tiān kōng lǐ de yī piàn yún, ǒu ěr tóu yǐng zài nǐ de bō xīn
literal: I · am · sky · in · 's · one · piece · cloud, by chance · cast · shadow · on · your · 's · wave · heart
natural: I am a cloud in the sky, by chance casting my shadow on the heart of your waters

meaning.en: Opening of Xu Zhimo's 'By Chance': two lives meet for a moment, like a cloud reflected on a lake, and then part.
meaning.zh: 徐志摩《偶然》的开头：两个人的相遇像天上的云偶然映在水面上，转瞬即逝。

equivalents: ships that pass in the night
a chance meeting that leaves only a shadow

examples.zh: 她轻声念起“我是天空里的一片云，偶尔投影在你的波心”。
examples.en: She softly recited 'I am a cloud in the sky, by chance casting my shadow on the heart of your waters'.

examples.zh: 朋友圈里有人配着湖面的照片，写下“我是天空里的一片云，偶尔投影在你的波心”。
examples.en: Someone in the group chat posted a lake photo captioned 'I am a cloud in the sky, by chance casting my shadow on the heart of your waters'.

story.en: Xu Zhimo (1897-1931) wrote 'By Chance' (《偶然》) in 1926, first as lines in the play 《卞昆冈》 and then as a separate poem.
story.zh: 徐志摩（1897—1931）1926年作《偶然》，最初出现在剧本《卞昆冈》中，后来单独成诗。

usage.en: Widely known; quoted for brief, bittersweet encounters, often in love or friendship. 波心 is the centre of the waves (the water's heart). The poem goes on: 你不必讶异，更无须欢喜，在转瞬间消灭了踪影.
usage.zh: 广为人知，多用于短暂而略带惆怅的相遇，常见于爱情和友情。“波心”指水波的中心。诗接着写道：“你不必讶异，更无须欢喜，在转瞬间消灭了踪影。”

text: 没有伟大的人物出现的民族，是世界上最可怜的生物之群
pinyin: méi yǒu wěi dà de rén wù chū xiàn de mín zú, shì shì jiè shàng zuì kě lián de shēng wù zhī qún
literal: not · have · great · 's · figure · appear · 's · nation, is · world · on · most · pitiable · 's · creature · 's · herd
natural: a nation in which no great figure appears is the most pitiable herd of creatures on earth

meaning.en: Yu Dafu's remark on Lu Xun's death: a people that produces no great men has nothing to look up to, and one that has them but does not honour them is hopeless.
meaning.zh: 郁达夫悼念鲁迅时所说：一个民族若没有伟大的人物，便是最可怜的；有了伟大人物而不知敬重，更是没有希望。

equivalents: a nation without great people is to be pitied
a people needs its heroes

examples.zh: 纪念展的序言引用了“没有伟大的人物出现的民族，是世界上最可怜的生物之群”。
examples.en: The preface to the memorial exhibition quoted 'a nation in which no great figure appears is the most pitiable herd of creatures on earth'.

examples.zh: 谈到如何对待文化名人，他想起了“没有伟大的人物出现的民族，是世界上最可怜的生物之群”这句话。
examples.en: Speaking of how to treat cultural figures, he recalled 'a nation in which no great figure appears is the most pitiable herd of creatures on earth'.

story.en: Yu Dafu (1896-1945) wrote 'Remembering Lu Xun' (《怀鲁迅》) in 1936, after Lu Xun's death in October that year.
story.zh: 郁达夫（1896—1945）在1936年10月鲁迅逝世后撰写《怀鲁迅》一文。

usage.en: Quoted in tributes to Lu Xun and in talk of respecting national heroes. The sentence goes on: 有了伟大的人物，而不知拥护，爱戴，崇仰的国家，是没有希望的奴隶之邦. 生物之群 is Yu's strong, rhetorical phrase for a herd of living things.
usage.zh: 多见于纪念鲁迅的文章和谈论尊重民族英才的场合。下文接着说：“有了伟大的人物，而不知拥护，爱戴，崇仰的国家，是没有希望的奴隶之邦。”“生物之群”是郁达夫语气强烈的说法。

text: 重新疆者所以保蒙古，保蒙古者所以卫京师
pinyin: zhòng xīn jiāng zhě suǒ yǐ bǎo méng gǔ, bǎo méng gǔ zhě suǒ yǐ wèi jīng shī
literal: value · Xinjiang · that · is how · protect · Mongolia, protect · Mongolia · that · is how · defend · capital
natural: valuing Xinjiang is how Mongolia is protected, and protecting Mongolia is how the capital is defended

meaning.en: Zuo Zongtang's strategic argument: Xinjiang shields Mongolia and Mongolia shields Beijing, so the northwest frontier must not be given up.
meaning.zh: 左宗棠的战略论述：新疆保护蒙古，蒙古保护京师，所以西北边疆不能放弃。

equivalents: the frontier protects the heartland
each province guards the next

examples.zh: 讲左宗棠收复新疆时，老师引用“重新疆者所以保蒙古，保蒙古者所以卫京师”。
examples.en: Teaching Zuo Zongtang's recovery of Xinjiang, the teacher quoted 'valuing Xinjiang is how Mongolia is protected, and protecting Mongolia is how the capital is defended'.

examples.zh: 展板上写着“重新疆者所以保蒙古，保蒙古者所以卫京师”，概括了他的边防思想。
examples.en: The display board carries 'valuing Xinjiang is how Mongolia is protected, and protecting Mongolia is how the capital is defended', summing up his frontier thinking.

story.en: In 1875, during the debate over whether to prioritise coastal defence or the northwest frontier, Zuo Zongtang (1812-1885) argued in a memorial to the throne that holding Xinjiang was essential to the safety of Mongolia and the capital.
story.zh: 1875年，朝廷就海防与塞防孰先孰后展开争论，左宗棠（1812—1885）在奏折中指出守住新疆对保卫蒙古和京师至关重要。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of the 1870s 'maritime defence versus frontier defence' (海防塞防) debate and of the history of Xinjiang. The memorial goes on to say that the northwest is 'like arm and fingers joined' (臂指相连).
usage.zh: 多在谈论1870年代“海防与塞防之争”和新疆历史时引用。奏折下文说西北“臂指相连，形势完整”。

text: 能变则全，不变则亡；全变则强，小变仍亡
pinyin: néng biàn zé quán, bù biàn zé wáng, quán biàn zé qiáng, xiǎo biàn réng wáng
literal: can · change · then · survive whole, not · change · then · perish; fully · change · then · strong, slightly · change · still · perish
natural: if you can change, you survive intact; if you do not, you perish; change fully and you grow strong; change a little and you still perish

meaning.en: Kang Youwei's warning in 1898: only thorough reform can save the state; half-measures end in ruin just the same.
meaning.zh: 康有为1898年的警告：只有彻底变法才能救国，小修小补同样会走向灭亡。

equivalents: change or die
half-measures are no better than none

examples.zh: 他在发言中引用“能变则全，不变则亡；全变则强，小变仍亡”，主张彻底改革公司制度。
examples.en: In his speech he quoted 'change and survive whole, refuse and perish; change fully and grow strong, change a little and still perish' to argue for thorough reform of the company.

examples.zh: 讲戊戌变法时，课件上打出了“能变则全，不变则亡；全变则强，小变仍亡”。
examples.en: In the lesson on the 1898 Reform the slide showed 'change and survive whole, refuse and perish; change fully and grow strong, change a little and still perish'.

origin.source: 康有为《上清帝第六书》（1898年）

story.en: Kang Youwei (1858-1927) presented his sixth memorial to the Guangxu Emperor in January 1898, urging comprehensive reform, which led to the Hundred Days' Reform that summer.
story.zh: 1898年1月，康有为（1858—1927）向光绪帝呈上第六书，请求全面变法，同年夏天爆发了百日维新。

usage.en: Often quoted in discussions of reform and corporate or institutional change as an argument for thoroughness. Written in a balanced four-part classical pattern. 全 here means whole, intact.
usage.zh: 常用于谈改革，也用于企业和机构变革，强调改革要彻底。四句对举，是典型的文言句式。“全”在这里指完整、保全。
